collections.title: Trika prep week
collections.author: Wiser
collections.intro: Seven days of foundation for Abhinavagupta and VBT study: steady breath, the turn of the breath, and recognition. Ten minutes a day. Initiated practices are not here: when the gap is steady, take the next step with a qualified teacher in the tradition.

units.title: Settle
units.intro: The home base: ease through the body with the breath.

items.note: Where is the breath clearest today? That is your seat for the week.

units.title: The turn
units.intro: Notice where the in-breath becomes the out-breath. Rest there; hold nothing.

items.note: Did you find the turning, or the idea of it? Either is fine — noted, not judged.

units.title: Recognition
units.intro: One sutra slowly, then look: does anything appear outside awareness?

items.note: Write one sentence on what recognition felt like versus what you thought about it.

units.title: Return to ease
units.intro: Same foundation, deeper seat. The gap work needs a rested body.

items.note: Compare today with day 1: steadier, sleepier, brighter? Log it plainly.

units.title: Longer turn
units.intro: Same gap practice, full sit. Let attention fall in; never force it.

items.note: If strain appears, drop back to ease. The gap is found, not made.

units.title: Recognition again
units.intro: Same contemplation, fresh experience. Sound, thought, feeling — inside or outside?

items.note: One line for the journal: what was recognised, and by what?

units.title: The week in one sit
units.intro: Ease, then the turn, then recognition — one short sit chaining all three in order.

items.note: Which of the three is your door? That is what you take to a teacher next.
